children: Saudi Arabia’s Dammam Airports Company announced on Sunday that it has appointed Canada-based global engineering consultancy firm WSP the design mandate for the expansion and development of King Fahd International Airport.

The contract covers the expansion of passenger terminals and airport facilities, improvements to airport entrances and access roads, upgrades to baggage-handling systems and passenger guidance systems within the terminals, the Dammam Airports said in a social media post
The contract value and duration wasn’t disclosed.

The airport's master plan aims to increase capacity to more than 19.3 million passengers per year by 2030, with capacity subsequently rising to 32 million passengers annually. The plan also targets annual air cargo capacity of more than 600,000 tonnes and operational capacity of up to 77 aircraft movements per hour.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
